reasoning: The target-resolution, context filtering, etymology, and wordplay rules already cover the other failures, so repeating them would not patch a skill gap. A narrow clarification can prevent over-shortening supported names when a clue shows only part of a conventional name or the answer includes a supported honorific.

edits.target: Return only the identifying portion requested: do not repeat title wording already supplied by the clue or append a generic class word when it is implicit, unless the full name is requested or needed to distinguish the answer.
edits.content: Return only the identifying portion requested, but distinguish the named entity from a gap in its wording: when a clue uses a blank or partial form of a conventional proper name (including paired names such as “___ & [name]”) and asks for that entity, return its full supported conventional name rather than automatically giving only the omitted token. Give only the token when the prompt explicitly asks for the missing word itself. For personal names, preserve source-supported conventional honorifics (such as “Sir”) and other identifying elements; omit generic labels and unsupported additions.
